AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #14
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Establishment Planting Site? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Establishment Planting Site.

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Controlling Soil Pollution? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Controlling Soil Pollution.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Controlling Soil Pollution.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Controlling Soil Pollution.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Controlling Soil Pollution.

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparing Animal Products 9 2.4 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene.

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production ? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Selected Crop Management Practises? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Selected Crop Management Practises.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Selected Crop Management Practises.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Selected Crop Management Practises.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Selected Crop Management Practises.

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr? (1 mark)

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.

   B. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Food Nutrients.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Food Nutrients.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Food Nutrients.

14. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

15. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

16. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 0 °C

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparing Animal Products? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparing Animal Products.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparing Animal Products.

18. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food? (1 mark)

   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food.

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Trees? (1 mark)

   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Trees.

   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene in Rearing Animals.

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Constructing Water Retention Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Constructing Water Retention Structures.

22. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
